info.desc: "Evil Empire" is the second album by Rage Against the Machine. Released on April 16, 1996, almost four years after the band's first, self-titled album named Rage Against the Machine. The album's title is taken from the phrase "Evil Empire", which was used by former U.S. President Ronald Reagan and many Western conservatives in describing the former Soviet Union. The track "Bulls on Parade" became the first single and, as with their debut, five singles were released in total. "Evil Empire" debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200. The song "Tire Me" won the 1996 Grammy award for Best Metal .

podcast.body: Released in 1996, the album's title "Evil Empire" directly references a Ronald Reagan speech where he described the Soviet Union as such, but the band politically reinterpreted it to apply to the United States. The cover features an altered 1940s/50s painting by Mel Ramos of a boy named Ari Messle, originally a comic hero "Crime Buster," with the "C" on his chest changed to an "E" and the caption changed to "Evil Empire." "First the title, it comes from a Ronald Reagan speech where he called the Soviet Union just that the evil empire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Stories Behind Iconic Album Covers Part 2

podcast.body: Released on April 16, 1996, nearly four years after the band's debut record. The album debuted at number one on the album charts and sold millions of copies, with some of its songs being nominated for Grammy Awards. The lengthy gap between the debut and this album was due to extensive touring, non-album projects like movie soundtracks, and significant internal politics and dissension within the highly political band. An earlier attempt to record the album in Atlanta in late 1994, where 20 songs were written over four to five months, was aborted due to "tensions and creative differences." Recording eventually resumed in Hollywood and Melbourne, Australia. "Evil Empire came out in April 1996 and debuted at number one on the album charts."

podcast.body: This album was being promoted when the band had a major incident during a scheduled performance on Saturday Night Live. Their intention to protest a Republican presidential candidate led to censorship and their eventual expulsion from the studio. "Tenemos ese grandísimo incidente que tuvieron cuando estaban sacando su segundo álbum, cuando vivan actuar en el Sator de Ney-Live y nos llegaban a actuar completamente censurados y los acababan echando la gente de suuridad del Sator de Ney-Live."
